chapter: The district underworld and street musicians
title: The Big 25: Frank Keelan's fight and hitting a madam with a cue stick
summary: Dawson tells of gambling at the Big 25, Big Zack beating Frank Keelan, and hitting a man with a cue stick who turned out to be a wealthy madam.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, you know, John Lawler told me a lot of boxers used to hang out by the, uh, Big 25.

Yeah. That was good. See, trying a long, long time ago, that's where they used to have all them big coach games, around 25. Frank Keelan was a trumpet player. He used to gamble at 25. And they had a big guy called Zack, Big, Big Zack, big black fella. Him and Frank Keelan got in a humbug, caught Frank messing around with a deck of cards,

And he hit Frank Keelan, he burst Frank Keelan in the nose and mouth and everything. I mean, they had a big, had a terrible, he was powerful, strong and, than Frank. But Frank had been drinking Frank like his liquor. Frank was half drunk. He took advantage of him. That's what I, I didn't like, you see, cause Zack took advantage of Frank Keelan. You see, at the corner they had a clothing store at that corner, Canal Street, they wear Krauses there now. I had to go there and get him a shirt, brand new shirt. All his old shirt, what he had on was just full of blood, you know. So, uh, yeah, everybody went to cry out soon. That was, uh, that was the headquarters for all the positioners used to hang out right there.
And the ladies hats are still beautiful there, they say. Yeah.

At 25's was a great place there. Now I hit Amorphedi one time in 25, yeah. Amorphedi, he, he got, I don't know, I was, I was dressed nice and all the time, you know. And so me, Felix King and all them big gamblers, we always at the counter drinking liquor. Well I, W, Hartford then time was, you could get a whole fifth or down the quarter. I, W, oh, good boy even whiskey. So this old Norfolk and I come in there and he, he, he was watching me, and I didn't know it, but I was playing pool, cause I had the queues, 20 ounce, 20 ounce queues stick in my hand, you know, and stuff, and go get us a drink, you know. And he come and grab me round the neck, oh, sugar, you saw it, and kiss me when he did that for a long, I read around the neck, love off. You hit him with a.
I hit him with a cue stick. Well.
And knock him down there. Think Andrew Jepson tell you about that. He fell down on the floor, he say, oh, you're a cruel thing.
Well did you make him happy when you hit him?

He just laid there. The Henry Bowser was a bartender. Yeah. Henry Bowser, cause I was fixing to hit him another league, so I just jumped over the counter and grab him. I said, man, you know who you hit? I said, I don't give a damn who I hit with or I don't care about it. He said, you hit one of the best guys around you. Boy, that man is crazy about you, you could get anything you want from him. I said, I ain't studying nothing. Was he rich? He was rich? Oh, but he was, he was, he was a big shot around there, big shot, you know, small for that. And he was, he handled good money. So that's why Henry told me, I didn't know nothing about him, you know, but Henry told me after I found out, you know, he had a big house that he had was renting and was running a house just like the women had.
Oh, he was a madam. He was a madam of the house.
They had all different morphed out, they lived in there with him. But he was in the money. And I didn't know it, you see.
